answer:
The recurring onboarding blockers appearing across the playbook and implementation data are threefold:

1. **Permission Mapping** (accounts for 45% of delay incidents): Synchronizing a customer's RBAC/Active Directory group or folder permissions into NovaLearn frequently results in configuration errors, halting go-live validation [NL-031#NL-031-S04] [NL-012#NL-012-S06]. The playbook explicitly identifies permission mapping as the most common blocker and details the directory sync procedures and error handling for group duplication and cyclical inheritance [NL-005#NL-005-S06].

2. **Source Ingestion Cleanup** (accounts for 30% of delays): Customers dump outdated, redundant, or corrupted files into the platform, requiring a paused onboarding while they manually audit and purge their corpus [NL-031#NL-031-S04] [NL-012#NL-012-S06]. The playbook addresses this in Phase 3 (Data Cleanup) with the gate requirement of archiving stale documents [NL-005#NL-005-S02].

3. **OCR and Scanned PDFs** (accounts for 25% of delays): Image-only PDF policy manuals return incomplete citations because the standard parser fails to detect text layers, failing the 85% citation correctness threshold [NL-031#NL-031-S04] [NL-012#NL-012-S06]. The playbook acknowledges this by provisioning a dedicated, high-priority OCR processing queue for enterprise customers with high volumes of scanned heritage PDFs and requiring OCR for legacy documents [NL-005#NL-005-S02] [NL-005#NL-005-S09].

These match the historical delay data (e.g., BrightPath Healthcare at 9.5 weeks due to OCR/compliance, Acme Manufacturing at 5.4 weeks due to AD sync) [NL-012#NL-012-S06].
